name: Nassau Glass Co Ltd
brand_truth: The Bahamas' first glass fabricator, on the same hill on Mackey Street since 1959.
buyer: Nassau homeowners renovating bathrooms and kitchens, landlords and property managers, designers and contractors; walk-in customers for fans, bulbs and framing.

design.signature: Real-time 3D float-glass slab (transmission, chromatic aberration) refracting warm and cool light bars and a hanging bulb; glass measure helper that draws the pane to proportion and writes the call summary; department filter

current_site_findings: 'SASTIFIED CLIENTS' misspelled in large letters on the homepage.
Many photos are stock images (one filename still says Unsplash).
No homepage meta description; title is just 'Nassau Glass Company'.
Services carousel repeats the same six departments twice.
A 'business for sale' notice sits beside the phone numbers on every page.
pitch_line: Nassau's first glass company deserves better than stock photos and a misspelled 'SASTIFIED CLIENTS'; this concept shows glass and light the way you sell them and helps customers measure before they call, which also strengthens the business for its next owner.

qa.note: 3D scene is heavy under software GL in the sandbox; rendering pauses when off-screen and under reduced motion

assumptions: Department one-line descriptions are paraphrased from their department names and homepage blurbs
Measure helper asks only item, size, quantity and location (no glass types or edge finishes listed on their site)
notes: Record said no site; nassauglass.com is live (WordPress). The business is advertised for sale on its own site (contact Andrew Rogers): pitch the owner on sale value, or approach the buyer once known. Their photos were stock, so none used. No email found; enquiry is phone-led (two numbers + international).
